title: person.json — a person the database holds, projected
description:
People are shared by the items that credit them, so they are a category of their own beside movies/ and series/, with the same id-based folders and the same shard:

  people/<aa>/<personId>/person.json
  people/<aa>/<personId>/<content hash>.<ext>   the images it lists

<aa> is the first two characters of the id. Like metadata.json this is a projection, not a record: what the catalog database held about the person at the moment asOf names — the person's row as databaseUpdatedAt says it was last modified, with the reference data as fresh as sources says — written by the one service that owns people and replaced whole on every projection, so nothing is merged. There is no checksums file beside it, on purpose: a checksum written with one projection would be wrong after the next, and each image is named by the hash of its own bytes, so its name is its check. A rebuild restores the person exactly as the last projection left it, so a biography and a portrait survive the loss of the database.

There is no list of credits: which items credit a person is what those items' metadata.json says, by personId, and repeating it here would make every new credit rewrite this file. A credit whose person has no folder here is not an error — the person may not have been projected yet — and a validator says so as a note.

personId.description: Equals the name of the folder this file sits in, its first two characters are the shard folder, and it is the personId every credit of this person carries. Stable: person pages are user-facing URLs keyed by it.

asOf.description: The state of the database this file is a projection of. A later projection replaces the whole file.

databaseUpdatedAt.description: The modification time of the person's database row this projection reflects, as defs.schema.json describes it. A person changes more often than an item does — a new role, a death, a new photo — so this is what tells a person record that went stale from a current one.

name.description: The person's current name, as the database displays it. A credit records the name as it was for its title — it may be the one the person went by then — and a reader prefers this one wherever the person has a record.

sortName.description: The name as it sorts, e.g. 'Hubert, Ian'.

alsoKnownAs.description: Other names the person is known by: a birth name, a stage name, the name in another script.

deathDate.description: Not before birthDate, as far as both are known.

knownForDepartment.description: The department the reference database says the person is best known for — 'Acting', 'Directing', 'Writing' — in its words. A hint for ordering what a person page shows, not a credit: the credits stay the items'.

biography.description: The biography in every language the database holds it in, keyed by BCP 47 language — 'und' when the database does not record which language its text is in. A reader picks the variant for its viewer the way it picks a localized title.

externalIds.description: Explicit, unambiguous keys into reference databases, enough to fetch the person's texts and images again.

imdb.description: A person id, which starts 'nm'; a title id ('tt…') is not one.

images.description: Every image file in this folder that the projection uses, beside person.json. An image a later projection stops naming is left to be swept (library-v2-sweep.py). At most one portrait is primary: the one a person page shows.
